title: GEOLOGIC MAP OF THE NOACHIS QUADRANGLE OF MARS By E. Peterson James 1977

legend_data.value: Contact - Queried where location or existence highly uncertain
Fault-Line at crest of scarp; dashed where approximately located. Bar and ball on downdip side. Locally serves as contact
legend_data.key_data: solid_line with bar and ball on downdip side

legend_data.value: High, steep, narrow ridge at crest; dashed where approximately located. Interpretation: Remnant of rotated upthrown fault block

Low, gently sloping, broad ridge; Line at crest; dashed where approximately located. Locally serves as approximately located contact. Interpretation: Most probably structurally controlled volcanic fissure complexes

Asymmetric ridge - Hachures on broadly sloping side; barb points to steep, narrow side. Line at crest. Interpretation: Probably fault-controlled volcanic fissure complex with post-volcanism fault rejuvenation
legend_data.key_data: solid_line with hachures on one side

legend_data.value: Scarp - Line at crest; dashed where approximately located. Barb down slopes. Interpretation: Most probably fault scars, some possibly erosional scars, some possibly lava-flow fronts

Trough - Narrow linear or arcuate depression. Line at bottom; dashed where approximately located. Interpretation: Some probably graben, some probably collapse depressions, some possibly erosional channels
Channel - Narrow sinuous depression in dendritic system. Line at bottom; dashed where approximately located. Interpretation: Formed by fluvial erosion

Lineament - Straight or arcuate feature of indeterminate relief. Locally serves as approximately located contact. Interpretation: Various origins such as fault scarps, erosional scarps and troughs, perhaps some low ridges
Circular depression - Rimless crater at summit of shield or dome. Some nearly filled. Interpretation: Caldera
Irregular depression - Broad, rimless. Interpretation: Formed by collapse
Prominent rim crest - Dashed where approximately located. Mapped only for elevated crater material and where other crater units are subdivided. Locally serves as contact
Buried rim crest - Queried where existence uncertain

Basin ring - Dotted where buried by shield. Structures including ridges, scarps, and mountains. Three Hellas rings numbered from basin center or basin ring in northwest part of unnumbered region. Basin ring formed by faulting caused by gravitational collapse of surrounding areas toward deep initial impact crater

Dark material - Splotches and streaks related to topography, many located on crater floors. Outlines vary from nearly circular to very irregular. Interpretation: Some deposits of dark eolian sediments, locally forming dune fields; some areas of dark rock exposed by deflation or nondeposition of light surficial sediments
